# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster […]

### Signal (reactive state)

```rust
let mut count = use_signal(|| 0);

// Read
count();              // clone value (callable syntax)
count.read();         // Ref<T> borrow
count.peek();         // read WITHOUT subscribing

// Write
count.set(5);         // replace
count += 1;           // arithmetic assignment
*count.write() = 10;  // mutable guard, triggers re-render on drop
```

pages:

- `https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files`
- `https://tailwindcss.com/docs/functions-and-directives`

Tailwind changes class syntax and editor diagnostics between releases; do not
guess when an editor warning, new variant, or v4 migration detail is involved.

## Class Authoring Rules

- Prefer built-in variants over arbitrary variants. Use `hover:`, `focus:`,
  `focus-visible:`, `disabled:`, `aria-disabled:`, `data-ars-selected:`, and
  `group-data-ars-selected:` before reaching for bracketed selectors.
- For presence-only `data-*` attributes, use the v4 named data variant:
  `data-ars-selected:bg-blue-600`, not the bracketed arbitrary-selector form.
  For parent group state, use `group-data-ars-selected:bg-white/20`, not
  the bracketed group-data form.

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct TabItemContext<K: TabKey> {
    item: TabRenderItem<K>,
}

/// Typed render item supplied by [`List`] and [`Panels`] when rendering
/// tab-scoped parts.
///
/// The item carries the adapter row data selected from the root
/// [`TabsSource`]. Consumers can pass it to [`TabShell`] or [`Panel`]
/// without repeating or stringifying tab keys.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct TabRenderItem<K: TabKey> {
    /// Row data for this tab in the current collection order.
    pub tab: Tab<K>,
}

impl<K: TabKey> TabRenderItem<K> {
    /// Returns the typed key for this render item.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn key(&self) -> K {
        self.tab.key
    }
}

/// Dioxus Tabs root part.

fn tab_shell_provides_item_context_to_trigger_and_close_trigger() {
    fn app() -> Element {
        rsx! {
            tabs::Root {
                default_value: "first",

                    let mut rows = three_tabs();
                    rows[0] = rows[0].clone().closable(true);

                tabs::List::<StrKey> {
                    tab_row: |item: tabs::TabRenderItem<StrKey>| rsx! {
                        tabs::TabShell { item, class: "test-tabs__shell",
                            tabs::Trigger::<StrKey> { class: "test-tabs__trigger" }
                            tabs::CloseTrigger::<StrKey> { class: "test-tabs__close" }
                        }
                    },
                }
                tabs::Panels::<StrKey> {}
            }
        }
    }

    let html = render_app(app);

    assert!(
        html.contains(r#"class="test-tabs__trigger""#),
        "trigger should render from TabShell context: {html}"
    );
    assert!(
        html.contains(r#"class="test-tabs__close""#),
        "close trigger should render from TabShell context: {html}"
    );
    assert!(
        html.contains(r#"aria-label="Close First""#),
        "close trigger should receive the contextual row label: {html}"
    );
    assert!(
        html.contains(r#"data-ars-part="tab-shell""#)
            && html.contains(r#"data-ars-selected"#)
            && html.contains(r#"data-ars-closable"#),
        "selected closable shell should mirror row state for direct styling: {html}"
    );
}

The suspicious point is now concrete: custom `tab_row` renderers return a `TabShell` without a stable Dioxus component key, while the default path adds one. When rows are closable/reorderable and selection changes, Dioxus can reuse the wrong component instance by position, which matches “previously selected closable row loses its trigger content.” I’m going to add a regression around the custom renderer path before patching.

fn document() -> web_sys::Document {
    web_sys::window()

        .expect("document should exist")
}

fn container() -> web_sys::HtmlElement {
    let element = document()
        .create_element("div")
        .expect("container should be created");

    document()
        .body()
        .expect("body should exist")
        .append_child(&element)
        .expect("container should be attached");

    element
        .dyn_into::<web_sys::HtmlElement>()
        .expect("container should be an HtmlElement")
}

fn add_indicator_measurement_styles(parent: &web_sys::HtmlElement) {
    let style = document()
        .create_element("style")
        .expect("style element should be created");

    style.set_text_content(Some(
        r#"
            [data-ars-part="list"] {
                display: inline-flex !important;
                align-items: center !important;
            }

            [data-ars-part="list"][aria-orientation="vertical"] {
                flex-direction: column !important;
                align-items: flex-start !important;
            }

            [data-ars-part="tab"] {
                display: inline-flex !important;
                width: auto !important;
            }
        "#,
    ));

    parent
        .append_child(&style)
        .expect("indicator measurement style should append");
}

#[wasm_bindgen_test(async)]
async fn web_inline_array_close_trigger_removes_owned_tab() {
    let parent = container();
    let dom = VirtualDom::new(inline_owned_close_probe);

    dioxus_web::launch::launch_virtual_dom(
        dom,
        dioxus_web::Config::new().rootelement(parent.clone().into()),
    );

    animation_frame_turn().await;
    animation_frame_turn().await;

    let close = parent
        .query_selector(r#"[data-ars-part="tab-close-trigger"]"#)
        .expect("query should succeed")
        .expect("close trigger should render")
        .dyn_into::<web_sys::HtmlElement>()
        .expect("close trigger is HtmlElement");

    click(&close);

    animation_frame_turn().await;

    assert_eq!(
        first_with_data_part(&parent, "list")
            .query_selector_all(r#"[role="tab"]"#)
            .expect("query should succeed")
            .length(),
        2,
        "inline array tabs should remove through the adapter-owned store"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        selected_tab_text(&parent),
        "Third",
        "closing the selected owned tab should select the successor"
    );
}

    let status = parent
        .query_selector("#owned-panel-status")
        .expect("query should succeed")
        .expect("status element should exist")
        .text_content()
        .unwrap_or_default();

    assert_eq!(
        status, "updated",
        "owned inline tabs must refresh existing panel content when parent Dioxus state changes"
    );
}

#[wasm_bindgen_test(async)]
async fn web_inline_array_owned_tabs_keep_refreshed_panel_after_close() {
    let parent = container();
    let dom = VirtualDom::new(inline_owned_panel_close_after_refresh_probe);

    dioxus_web::launch::launch_virtual_dom(
        dom,
        dioxus_web::Config::new().rootelement(parent.clone().into()),
    );

    animation_frame_turn().await;
    animation_frame_turn().await;

    assert_eq!(selected_panel_text(&parent), "initial");

    click(
        &parent
            .query_selector("#update-owned-panel-before-close")
            .expect("query should succeed")
            .expect("update trigger should exist")
            .dyn_into::<web_sys::HtmlElement>()
            .expect("update trigger is HtmlElement"),
    );

    animation_frame_turn().await;

    assert_eq!(
        selected_panel_text(&parent),
        "updated",
        "parent same-key render content should refresh before close"
    );

    click(&first_with_data_part(&parent, "tab-close-trigger"));

    animation_frame_turn().await;

    assert_eq!(
        selected_panel_text(&parent),
        "updated",
        "closing another owned tab must not restore stale same-key panel content"
    );
}

I’m going to make the unselected trigger color explicit in the Tailwind templates/examples, keeping selected color state-owned by `data-ars-selected:text-white`.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster […]

# Dioxus 0.7.3 — Framework Reference

**Version:** 0.7.3 (latest stable as of 2026-03-18)
**Docs:** [docs.rs/dioxus](https://docs.rs/dioxus/0.7.3/dioxus/) | [dioxuslabs.com/learn/0.7](https://dioxuslabs.com/learn/0.7/)

> This skill covers the `dioxus`, `dioxus-hooks`, `dioxus-signals`, `dioxus-stores`, `dioxus-router`, `dioxus-fullstack`, and `dioxus-document` crates.

## Standard Import

```rust
use dioxus::prelude::*;
```

## Quick Patterns

### Signal (reactive state)

```rust
let mut count = use_signal(|| 0);

// Read
count();              // clone value (callable syntax)
count.read();         // Ref<T> borrow
count.peek();         // read WITHOUT subscribing

// Write
count.set(5);         // replace
count += 1;           // arithmetic assignment
*count.write() = 10;  // mutable guard, triggers re-render on drop
```

> AGENT

Fixed the reorder visual break.

Root cause: my previous `text-slate-700` fix was too blunt. In Tailwind’s generated cascade it could override `data-ars-selected:text-white`, so after reorder selected/unselected labels looked swapped or blank. I changed it to only apply on non-selected triggers:

`[&:not([data-ars-selected])]:text-slate-700`

That keeps selected tabs white and gives unselected tabs an explicit readable color.

I also added a Dioxus wasm regression for the reorder path:
- custom low-level parts
- closable tabs
- selected tab reordered
- selected styling attrs must follow the semantic tab key, not the old DOM position

> AGENT

You’re right. The visual symptoms are downstream of a Dioxus identity/rendering bug: the custom `tab_row` path lets the internal store reorder, but the returned row components are not keyed at the list boundary, so Dioxus can keep rendering/reusing the old positional subtree. I’m going to fix that in the adapter, not in Tailwind.

                },
            }
            tabs::Panels::<StaticStr> {}
            tabs::LiveRegion {}
        }
    }
}

fn LocalPanelState(id: &'static str, initial: &'static str) -> Element {
    let mut status = use_signal_sync(|| initial.to_owned());

    let updated = format!("{initial}-updated");

    rsx! {
        button { id: "update-{id}", onclick: move |_| status.set(updated.clone()), "Update" }
        p { id, "{status}" }
    }
}

> AGENT

You were right. This was not Tailwind-only.

The real Dioxus bug was in [crates/ars-dioxus/src/navigation/tabs.rs](/Users/ericson/.codex/worktrees/61ee/ars-ui/crates/ars-dioxus/src/navigation/tabs.rs): the default `List`/`Panels` render path keyed `TabShell`/`Panel`, but the custom `tab_row` / `panel` renderer path returned the consumer element unkeyed. After reorder, the core/store order changed, but Dioxus reused the old positional subtree, so the visual order and state got out of sync.

I fixed it by wrapping custom renderer output in a keyed `Fragment` using the semantic tab key. That preserves the single DOM anatomy while giving Dioxus the identity boundary it needs.

I also tightened the wasm regression so it now proves:
- dragging selected `Keyboard` before `Overview` changes the rendered DOM order to `Keyboard, Overview, Closable`
- selected styling attrs follow the `Keyboard` key after reorder
- custom closable parts still keep labels/state after selection changes

Verification:
- `cargo test -p ars-dioxus --test tabs`
- Dioxus wasm tests matching `web_custom_parts_keep_closable`
- `cargo check --manifest-path examples/widgets-dioxus-tailwind/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo check --manifest-path examples/widgets-leptos-tailwind/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo xfmt`
- `cargo xclippy` passed, with only the existing `block v0.1.6` future-incompat note

## My request for Codex:
What the previous fix attempts were doing then? Should we keep them?

> AGENT

The previous fixes were addressing real-looking symptoms, but not the root cause.

The Tailwind changes did two things:
- Replaced warning-prone `data-[ars-*]` forms with canonical Tailwind v4 `data-ars-*` forms. Keep this. It is just syntax cleanup and avoids editor warnings.
- Added readable non-selected trigger color, then changed it to `[&:not([data-ars-selected])]:text-slate-700` so it does not fight selected white text. Keep this too. It makes the template more robust, but it was only masking part of the visual fallout from the Dioxus keying bug.

The real fix is the latest Dioxus adapter change: keying custom `tab_row` and `panel` renderer output with `Fragment { key: ... }`. That is the one that fixes the broken reorder/render identity.

So yes, I’d keep the previous Tailwind cleanups, but classify them as style-template hardening, not the bug fix. The only part that was wrong was the intermediate plain `text-slate-700`; it has already been corrected to not-selected-only styling.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster […]

The evidence points to a CSS-state mismatch, not reorder logic: during pointer drag, the dragged trigger keeps `data-ars-focus-visible`, so the shell-level outline we just added remains visible while the selected/hover/active drag styles also apply. I’m going to suppress the focus outline only while that trigger is actively being dragged, then verify the CSS examples compile.

> AGENT

Yes. `:active` was the wrong signal for native HTML drag: browsers usually drop `:active` once the drag session starts, so the rule can miss the whole period where the drag image is captured.

Stronger hypothesis: the custom drag image clone is copying the focused `TabShell` with `data-ars-focus-visible` still inside it. Since the clone is marked with `data-ars-drag-image="tab"`, the right fix is to scrub focus-visible state from the drag preview itself, instead of trying to infer dragging from CSS `:active`.

#[cfg(all(feature = "web", target_arch = "wasm32"))]
fn set_tab_shell_drag_image(event: &dioxus::prelude::Event<DragData>) {
    let data = event.data();

    let Some(event) = data.downcast::<web_sys::DragEvent>() else {
        return;
    };

    let Some(data_transfer) = event.data_transfer() else {
        return;
    };

    let Some(target) = event.target().or_else(|| event.current_target()) else {
        return;
    };

    let Ok(target) = target.dyn_into::<web_sys::Element>() else {
        return;
    };

    let shell = target
        .closest(r#"[data-ars-part="tab-shell"]"#)
        .ok()
        .flatten()
        .or_else(|| target.parent_element());

    let Some(shell) = shell else {
        return;
    };

    let rect = shell.get_bounding_client_rect();

    let Some(preview) = append_tab_drag_preview(&shell) else {
        return;
    };

    let x = (rect.width() / 2.0).round() as i32;

fn set_tab_shell_drag_image(event: &web_sys::DragEvent) {
    let Some(target) = event.target().or_else(|| event.current_target()) else {
        return;
    };

    let Ok(target) = target.dyn_into::<web_sys::Element>() else {
        return;
    };

    let shell = target
        .closest(r#"[data-ars-part="tab-shell"]"#)
        .ok()
        .flatten()
        .or_else(|| target.parent_element());

    let Some(shell) = shell else {
        return;
    };

    let rect = shell.get_bounding_client_rect();

    let Some(preview) = append_tab_drag_preview(&shell) else {
        return;
    };

    let x = (rect.width() / 2.0).round() as i32;
    let y = (rect.height() / 2.0).round() as i32;

    set_drag_image_by_reflection(event, &preview, x, y);

    remove_tab_drag_preview_soon(preview);
}

struct DragImageCall {
    part: Option<String>,
    preview: Option<String>,
    has_close_trigger: bool,
    connected: bool,
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
}

struct DragImageSpy {
    calls: Rc<RefCell<Vec<DragImageCall>>>,
    prototype: wasm_bindgen::JsValue,
    original: wasm_bindgen::JsValue,
    _closure: wasm_bindgen::closure::Closure<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Element, i32, i32)>,
}

impl Drop for DragImageSpy {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        drop(js_sys::Reflect::set(
            &self.prototype,
            &wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_str("setDragImage"),
            &self.original,
        ));
    }
}

fn install_drag_image_spy() -> DragImageSpy {
    let constructor = js_sys::Reflect::get(
        &js_sys::global(),
        &wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_str("DataTransfer"),
    )
    .expect("DataTransfer constructor should be available");

    let prototype =
        js_sys::Reflect::get(&constructor, &wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_str("prototype"))
            .expect("DataTransfer prototype should be available");

    let original =
        js_sys::Reflect::get(&prototype, &wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_str("setDragImage"))
            .expect("setDragImage should be available");

    let calls = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::<DragImageCall>::new()));
    let closure_calls = Rc::clone(&calls);
    let closure = wasm_bindgen::closure::Closure::wrap(Box::new(
        move |image: web_sys::Element, x: i32, y: i32| {
            let part = image.get_attribute("data-ars-part");

            let preview = image.get_attribute("data-ars-drag-image");

            let has_close_trigger = image
                .query_selector(r#"[data-ars-part="tab-close-trigger"]"#)
                .expect("query should succeed")
                .is_some();

            let connected = image.is_connected();

            closure_calls.borrow_mut().push(DragImageCall {
                part,
                preview,
                has_close_trigger,
                connected,
                x,
                y,
            });
        },
    )
        as Box<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Element, i32, i32)>);

    js_sys::Reflect::set(
        &prototype,
        &wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_str("setDragImage"),
        closure.as_ref(),
    )
    .expect("setDragImage spy should install");

    DragImageSpy {
        calls,
        prototype,
        original,
        _closure: closure,
    }
}

I found the preview code: it deep-clones the live shell, marks it `data-ars-drag-image`, then passes that to `setDragImage`. So any focus-visible data attributes in the live shell are copied into the browser drag image unless we explicitly remove them. I’m adding that scrub and a regression assertion to both adapter wasm tests.

> AGENT

Yes, the better hypothesis was the drag preview clone.

The browser drag image is not the live tab. We clone the `TabShell`, mark it `data-ars-drag-image="tab"`, and pass that clone to `setDragImage`. The clone was copying `data-ars-focus-visible`, so the focus ring became part of the captured drag image. CSS `:active` could not reliably fix it because native drag drops `:active` during the drag session.

I fixed it at the adapter layer for both Dioxus and Leptos: the drag preview clone now strips `data-ars-focus-visible` from itself and all descendants before `setDragImage`, while leaving the live focused tab untouched. I also added wasm regression assertions for both adapters.

Verified:

- Dioxus focused wasm drag-image test passed
- Leptos focused wasm drag-image test passed
- `cargo test -p ars-dioxus --test tabs`
- `cargo test -p ars-leptos --features ssr --test tabs`
- CSS widget checks
- `cargo xfmt`
- `cargo xclippy`
- `git diff --check`

        }

        attrs

fn append_tab_drag_preview(shell: &web_sys::Element) -> Option<web_sys::Element> {
    let preview = shell
        .clone_node_with_deep(true)
        .ok()?
        .dyn_into::<web_sys::Element>()
        .ok()?;

    preview.set_attribute("data-ars-drag-image", "tab").ok()?;

        )
        .ok()?;

    web_sys::window()?
        .document()?
        .body()?
        .append_child(&preview)
        .ok()?;

    Some(preview)
}

> AGENT

Confirmed with a live browser probe.

Root cause had two parts:

1. The source fix was correct, but `dx serve` was running with `--hot-reload false`, so `localhost:4200` was still serving a stale bundle.
2. The stale bundle had already stripped `data-ars-focus-visible`, but was still copying `data-ars-selected` / `aria-selected` into the custom drag image clone, which produced the blue duplicate tab.

I restarted the Dioxus CSS server on port `4200` and re-ran the keyboard-focus then dragstart probe. The rebuilt page now shows:

- live tab still has `data-ars-focus-visible`, `data-ars-selected`, `aria-selected`
- drag preview clone has no focus-visible state
- drag preview clone has no selected state
- drag preview clone background is transparent and has no selected shadow

The `dx` server is running again at `http://localhost:4200/`. Refresh your browser and retry the same keyboard then drag sequence.

> AGENT

You’re right. The last fix overcorrected.

What the screenshot shows is two separate concerns:
1. The drag preview should still carry the selected TabShell visual, including the close affordance. Removing selected state from the clone made the drag image collapse into mostly text.
2. The live tab should not show its keyboard focus ring while it is being dragged. That needs a live dragging state, not selected-state scrubbing from the preview.

I’m going to restore selected state in the drag image, keep focus-visible scrub only for the clone, and add a `data-ars-dragging` marker on the live shell during drag so CSS can suppress the live focus ring only while dragging.

Fixed the overcorrection.

The current behavior on the rebuilt `localhost:4200` page is now:

- The custom drag image is again the full selected `TabShell` visual, including the close affordance.
- The drag image does not copy `data-ars-focus-visible`, so it does not carry the keyboard focus ring.
- The live shell gets `data-ars-dragging` during native drag, and the CSS focus-ring selector excludes that state, so the original tab does not keep the focus ring while dragging.
- `data-ars-dragging` is cleared on `dragend` / `drop`.

I verified this with a live Playwright probe against `http://localhost:4200/` after restarting `dx serve`; the probe showed selected preview state preserved, focus-visible absent from the preview, and live outline computed as `none` while dragging.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster […]

**Version:** 0.7.3 (latest stable as of 2026-03-18)
**Docs:** [docs.rs/dioxus](https://docs.rs/dioxus/0.7.3/dioxus/) | [dioxuslabs.com/learn/0.7](https://dioxuslabs.com/learn/0.7/)

## Standard Import

```rust
use dioxus::prelude::*;
```

## Quick Patterns

### Signal (reactive state)

```rust
let mut count = use_signal(|| 0);

// Read
count();              // clone value (callable syntax)
count.read();         // Ref<T> borrow
count.peek();         // read WITHOUT subscribing

// Write
count.set(5);         // replace
count += 1;           // arithmetic assignment
*count.write() = 10;  // mutable guard, triggers re-render on drop
```

# Leptos 0.8.17 — Framework Reference

**Version:** 0.8.17 (latest stable as of 2026-03-18)
**Docs:** [docs.rs/leptos](https://docs.rs/leptos/0.8.17/leptos/) | [book.leptos.dev](https://book.leptos.dev)

## Standard Import

```rust
use leptos::prelude::*;
```

## Quick Patterns

### Signals (read-only + write-only pair)

```rust
let (count, set_count) = signal(0i32);       // ReadSignal + WriteSignal (both Copy)
set_count.set(5);
set_count.update(|n| *n += 1);
let val = count.get();                        // clone + subscribe
```

`ReadSignal<T>` is **read-only**. `WriteSignal<T>` is **write-only**. They are separate types.

For a combined read+write handle, use `RwSignal`:

```rust
let count = RwSignal::new(0i32);             // single handle, read + write
count.set(1); […]

#[cfg(all(feature = "web", target_arch = "wasm32"))]
fn set_tab_shell_drag_image(event: &dioxus::prelude::Event<DragData>) {
    let data = event.data();

    let Some(event) = data.downcast::<web_sys::DragEvent>() else {
        return;
    };

    let Some(data_transfer) = event.data_transfer() else {
        return;
    };

    let Some(target) = event.target().or_else(|| event.current_target()) else {
        return;
    };

    let Ok(target) = target.dyn_into::<web_sys::Element>() else {
        return;
    };

    let shell = target
        .closest(r#"[data-ars-part="tab-shell"]"#)
        .ok()
        .flatten()
        .or_else(|| target.parent_element());

    let Some(shell) = shell else {
        return;
    };

    blur_drag_source(&target);

    let rect = shell.get_bounding_client_rect();

    let Some(preview) = append_tab_drag_preview(&shell) else {
        return;
    };

    let x = (rect.width() / 2.0).round() as i32;
    let y = (rect.height() / 2.0).round() as i32;

    data_transfer.set_drag_image(&preview, x, y);

    remove_tab_drag_preview_soon(preview);
}

#[cfg(not(all(feature = "web", target_arch = "wasm32")))]

    preview.set_attribute("data-ars-drag-image", "tab").ok()?;
    preview.set_attribute("aria-hidden", "true").ok()?;
    scrub_drag_preview_focus_visible(&preview);
    preview
        .set_attribute(
            "style",
            "position: fixed; left: 0; top: 0; transform: translate(-10000px, -10000px); \
             pointer-events: none; z-index: -1;",
        )
        .ok()?;

    web_sys::window()?
        .document()?
        .body()?
        .append_child(&preview)
        .ok()?;

    Some(preview)
}

#[wasm_bindgen_test(async)]
async fn web_signal_backed_reorderable_updates_attrs_and_blocks_stale_drop() {
    let parent = container();
    let reordered = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<TestReorderEvent>::new()));
    let dom = VirtualDom::new_with_props(
        dynamic_reorderable_probe,
        DragReorderProbeProps {
            reordered: Arc::clone(&reordered),
        },
    );

    dioxus_web::launch::launch_virtual_dom(
        dom,
        dioxus_web::Config::new().rootelement(parent.clone().into()),
    );

    animation_frame_turn().await;
    animation_frame_turn().await;

    assert_eq!(
        tab_at(&parent, 0).get_attribute("draggable").as_deref(),
        Some("false")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        tab_at(&parent, 0).get_attribute("aria-roledescription"),
        None
    );

    first_with_id(&parent, "enable-reorder").click();

    animation_frame_turn().await;

    assert_eq!(
        tab_at(&parent, 0).get_attribute("draggable").as_deref(),
        Some("true")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        tab_at(&parent, 0)
            .get_attribute("aria-roledescription")
            .as_deref(),
        Some("draggable tab")
    );

    let first = tab_at(&parent, 0);
    let third = tab_at(&parent, 2);

    dispatch_drag_event(&first, "dragstart");

    first_with_id(&parent, "disable-reorder").click();

    animation_frame_turn().await;

    assert_eq!(
        tab_at(&parent, 0).get_attribute("draggable").as_deref(),
        Some("false")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        tab_at(&parent, 0).get_attribute("aria-roledescription"),
        None
    );

    let dragover = dispatch_drag_event(&third, "dragover");
    let drop = dispatch_drag_event(&third, "drop");

    assert!(
        !dragover.default_prevented(),
        "dragover should not accept a stale source after reorderable turns off"
    );
    assert!(
        !drop.default_prevented(),
        "drop should not reorder after reorderable turns off"

  present throughout the reorderable state, NOT only during drag).

### 6.2 Additional Event for reorderable tabs

`ReorderTab { tab: Key, new_index: usize }` is part of the base `Event`
enum (see §1.5).

### 6.3 Behavior for reorderable tabs

- **Drag and Drop is adapter-only.** Pointer-driven drag interaction
  (drag sources, drop targets, drop indicators, custom drag images) lives
  entirely in the framework adapter using its native drag
  infrastructure (`web_sys::DragEvent` + `Element::set_draggable` for
  the web). The custom drag image clones the public `TabShell` anatomy
  so the preview represents the dragged tab and adjacent close affordance
  without requiring widget-local preview policy. The agnostic core does
  not model drag state at all. On drop, the adapter computes a drag

```

# Post-implementation audit

This skill is the bridge between _"the named tests pass"_ and _"the user reviews the diff"_. It exists because the initial implementation of any task is usually correct on its surface acceptance criteria but quietly drifts from the spec, leaves untested defensive code, ships APIs that diverge from convention, or carries a fold-vs-lowercase mistake that won't surface until production. Running these audits before user-review collapses three reviewer round-trips into one.

The skill is mandatory per CLAUDE.md "Development Workflow" step 7 — run it after implementing any […]

Implemented the Tabs drag fix. Your lead was right: browser drag/drop belonged on `tabs::TabShell`, not just the trigger label.

Changed:
- Moved `draggable`, `dragstart`, `dragover`, `drop`, and `dragend` to `TabShell` in [Dioxus tabs](/Users/ericson/.codex/worktrees/61ee/ars-ui/crates/ars-dioxus/src/navigation/tabs.rs:890) and [Leptos tabs](/Users/ericson/.codex/worktrees/61ee/ars-ui/crates/ars-leptos/src/navigation/tabs.rs:874).
- Kept trigger-owned focus, keyboard, selection, ARIA, and refs.
- On dragstart, blur/scrub live `data-ars-focus-visible` from the shell subtree while preserving selected state in the drag image.
- Updated wasm tests so `draggable` is asserted on the shell, while `aria-roledescription` remains on the trigger.
- Updated Tabs specs to document `TabShell` as the browser drag source/drop target.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)

So this one is CSS/template suppression of native trigger focus, not machine state.

> AGENT

Fixed the click-after-keyboard-focus artifact.

Root cause: after clicking the focused tab, Chrome still matched `:focus-visible` on the trigger even though our `data-ars-focus-visible` state was cleared. The shell focus ring was correct, but the trigger’s native outline was leaking through.

Changed:
- [examples/widgets-dioxus-css/public/style.css](/Users/ericson/.codex/worktrees/61ee/ars-ui/examples/widgets-dioxus-css/public/style.css)
- [examples/widgets-leptos-css/assets/style.css](/Users/ericson/.codex/worktrees/61ee/ars-ui/examples/widgets-leptos-css/assets/style.css)

The tab trigger now always suppresses native outline, while the intended keyboard focus ring stays on `TabShell`. I also moved the grab cursor CSS from `[tab][draggable]` to `[tab-shell][draggable]`, matching the new shell-owned drag surface.

Verified:
- Live Playwright probe: trigger can still match `:focus-visible`, but computed `outline-style` is now `none`.
- `cargo xfmt`
- `cargo check --manifest-path examples/widgets-dioxus-css/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo check --manifest-path examples/widgets-leptos-css/Cargo.toml`
- `git diff --check`

Dioxus CSS gallery is rebuilt and running on `http://localhost:4200/`.

guess when an editor warning, new variant, or v4 migration detail is involved.

## Class Authoring Rules

  `data-ars-selected:bg-blue-600`, not the bracketed arbitrary-selector form.

  the bracketed group-data form.

.ars-tabs [data-ars-part="tab-shell"][data-ars-dragging],
.ars-tabs [data-ars-part="tab-shell"]:active {
    cursor: grabbing;
}

.ars-tabs [data-ars-part="tab-shell"][data-ars-dragging] * {
    cursor: grabbing;
}

.ars-tabs [data-ars-part="tab-shell"][data-ars-disabled] {
    cursor: not-allowed;
}

.ars-tabs
    [data-ars-part="tab-shell"]:has(
        > [data-ars-part="tab"][data-ars-focus-visible]
    ):not([data-ars-dragging]) {
    border-radius: 0.375rem;
    outline: 2px solid #2563eb;
    outline-offset: 2px;
}

.ars-tabs [data-ars-part="tab"] {
    appearance: none;
    border: 0;
    border-bottom: 2px solid transparent;
    background: transparent;
    color: #4b5563;
    cursor: pointer;
    font: inherit;
    outline: none;
    padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
}

.ars-tabs [data-ars-part="tab"][aria-selected="true"] {
    border-bottom-color: #2563eb;
    color: #111827;
}

.ars-tabs [data-ars-part="tab"][aria-disabled="true"] {
    color: #9ca3af;
    cursor: not-allowed;

# Tailwind v4

Use this skill before editing Tailwind class strings in Rust `view!` / `rsx!`
markup, styled source templates, widgets, or Tailwind CSS files.

## Current Docs Check

When syntax is uncertain, check the official Tailwind docs first. Prefer these
pages:

- `https://tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states`
- `https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files`
- `https://tailwindcss.com/docs/functions-and-directives`

Tailwind changes class syntax and editor diagnostics between releases; do not
guess when an editor warning, new variant, or v4 migration detail is involved.

## Class Authoring Rules

- Prefer built-in variants over arbitrary variants. Use `hover:`, `focus:`,
  `focus-visible:`, `disabled:`, `aria-disabled:`, `data-ars-selected:`, and
  `group-data-ars-selected:` before reaching for bracketed selectors.
- For presence-only `data-*` attributes, use the v4 named data variant:
  `data-ars-selected:bg-blue-600`, not the bracketed arbitrary-selector form.
  For parent group state, use `group-data-ars-selected:bg-white/20`, not
  the bracketed group-data form.
- Use bracketed data variants only when the […]

---
name: post-implementation-audit
description: MANDATORY after every implementation task — runs three sequential audits on the new code (spec/impl drift, iterative "anything missing?", test coverage) and lands every finding in the same PR before the user-review step. Invoke as soon as an implementation task's named tests pass, OR when any of these phrases appears: "ready to present", "implementation is complete", "named tests pass", "before opening the PR", "ready for review". Skipping this audit leaves spec drift, untested defensive code, missing conventions, and silent contract violations in the merged PR.
---

# Post-implementation audit

This skill is the bridge between _"the named tests pass"_ and _"the user reviews the diff"_. It exists because the initial implementation of any task is usually correct on its surface acceptance criteria but quietly drifts from the spec, leaves untested defensive code, ships APIs that diverge from convention, or carries a fold-vs-lowercase mistake that won't surface until production. Running these audits before user-review collapses three reviewer round-trips into one.

The skill is mandatory per CLAUDE.md "Development Workflow" step 7 — run it after implementing any […]

Stop when:

- Two consecutive rounds surface no new findings, **OR**

# Writing Skills

## Overview

**Writing skills IS Test-Driven Development applied to process documentation.**

**Personal skills live in agent-specific directories (`~/.claude/skills` for Claude Code, `~/.agents/skills/` for Codex)** 

You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch an agent fail without the skill, you don't know if the skill teaches the right thing.

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** You MUST understand superpowers:test-driven-development before using this skill. That skill defines the fundamental RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle. This skill adapts TDD to documentation.

**Official guidance:** For Anthropic's official skill authoring best practices, see anthropic-best-practices.md. This document provides additional patterns and guidelines that complement the TDD-focused approach in this skill.

## What is a Skill?

A **skill** is a reference guide for proven techniques, patterns, or tools. Skills help future Claude instances find and apply effective approaches.

**Skills are:** Reusable techniques, patterns, tools, reference guides

> AGENT

Yes. I’d add three concrete lessons.

1. **Cursor state is part of visual parity**
   Add to adapter docs: for draggable compound parts, verify cursor behavior for every interactive subpart, not only the semantic trigger. In Tabs terms: `TabShell`, `Trigger`, and `CloseTrigger` must agree on `pointer` at rest and `grabbing` while dragging.

2. **Drag state must override descendant cursors**
   Add to CSS/Tailwind guidance: when a public shell owns dragging, style the shell and descendants from the shell state:
   - CSS: `[data-ars-dragging], [data-ars-dragging] * { cursor: grabbing; }`
   - Tailwind: shell gets `data-ars-dragging:cursor-grabbing`; child parts get `group-data-ars-dragging:cursor-grabbing`.
   This avoids exactly what we saw: close trigger keeping `pointer` while the shell is dragging.

3. **Browser evidence should include computed cursor checks**
   Add to adapter visual/E2E checklist: browser proof for draggable components should inspect computed cursor on the drag source and all visible child controls before drag and during `data-ars-dragging`. Screenshots alone missed this until we probed computed styles.

The Tailwind skill should also explicitly mention cursor utilities as normal inline class state, not external CSS: `cursor-pointer`, `active:cursor-grabbing`, `data-ars-dragging:cursor-grabbing`, `group-data-ars-dragging:cursor-grabbing`, and `data-ars-disabled:cursor-not-allowed`.

## My request for Codex:
Can our tailwind examples use the high level tailwind components instead of the low level parts?

> AGENT

Yes, the Tailwind examples can use the high-level Tailwind components, and for the “normal gallery demo” they probably should.

The split we settled on is:

- `examples/widgets-*-tailwind`: should demonstrate the ready-made styled source-template component from `ars-*-components::navigation::tabs::tailwind::Tabs`.
- `examples/widgets-*` non-CSS/non-Tailwind: should demonstrate the low-level unstyled adapter primitives like `tabs::Root`, `tabs::List`, `tabs::TabShell`, `tabs::Trigger`, `tabs::CloseTrigger`, `tabs::Panels`, `tabs::Panel`, `tabs::LiveRegion`.
- Adapter tests / E2E fixtures: should still cover low-level primitives directly, because that proves the adapter API works without the styled wrapper.

So if our Tailwind widget examples are currently hand-composing low-level parts with large class strings, that is not ideal for the gallery. The Tailwind high-level component exists specifically so consumers can copy/edit that styled source template without rebuilding the primitive composition every time.

The one caveat: we should keep at least one low-level primitive example somewhere, but not in the Tailwind gallery path. That belongs in the unstyled examples or adapter fixtures.

//! This crate provides the checked-in reference styled components used by
//! widgets and future source-code distribution. Application authors who need
//! full ownership can compose the lower-level unstyled anatomy in

//! templates into user projects for shadcn-style customization.

    so we shouldn't do any `expect` for warnings on each component"
)]

//! Convenience re-exports for styled Dioxus components.

# GitHub Publish Changes

## Overview

Use this skill only when the user explicitly wants the full publish flow from the local checkout: branch setup if needed, staging, commit, push, and opening a pull request.

This workflow is hybrid:

- Use local `git` for branch creation, staging, commit, and push.
- Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for pull request creation after the branch is on the remote.
- Use `gh` as a fallback for current-branch PR discovery, auth checks, or PR creation when the connector path cannot infer the repository or head branch cleanly.

---
name: waiting-for-codex-review
description: Use immediately after pushing a PR to GitHub when Codex is configured to review the branch. Codex reviews asynchronously — it leaves a 👀 reaction on the PR while reviewing, drops the 👀 when the run finishes (either replacing it with 👍 if satisfied, or removing it and posting review threads if changes are needed). This skill defines the polling loop and the response workflow: wait for Codex's verdict, address any review threads it posts with the same rigor as `post-implementation-audit` (TDD + no coverage regression), commit, push, reply inline, resolve the thread, then keep waiting until 👍. Triggers on phrases like "wait for codex review", "what does codex say", "is codex done", "address the codex feedback", "check the PR reviews", or any post-push handoff where the user expects an automated reviewer's verdict. Invoke this skill even when the user does not explicitly name Codex — any GitHub PR where a 👀/👍 reaction signals an automated reviewer follows the same pattern.
---

  codex_eyes=$(echo "$reactions" | grep -E "codex.*:eyes$" || true)
  codex_thumb=$(echo "$reactions" | grep -E "codex.*:\+1$" || true)

  cur="reactions=[$reactions] threads=$threads"
  [ "$cur" != "$prev" ] && echo "[change] $cur"
  prev=$cur

  if [ -n "$codex_thumb" ]; then
    echo "VERDICT=approval"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ -z "$codex_eyes" ] && [ "$threads" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "VERDICT=needs_action threads=$threads"
    exit 0
  fi

  sleep 120
done

When this script completes via Bash `run_in_background`, the single completion
notification fires. Recover the verdict with one `Read` on the task's output
file — the last line is `VERDICT=approval` or `VERDICT=needs_action threads=N`.
If the file's last line is something else (script crashed or hit the bash
timeout), apply the defensive re-check below.

### Defensive re-check: don't trust silence as "still reviewing"

notifications back to the conversation is best-effort. If the runtime drops
the completion or change event, the loop sits waiting indefinitely for a

# Dioxus 0.7.3 — Framework Reference

**Version:** 0.7.3 (latest stable as of 2026-03-18)
**Docs:** [docs.rs/dioxus](https://docs.rs/dioxus/0.7.3/dioxus/) | [dioxuslabs.com/learn/0.7](https://dioxuslabs.com/learn/0.7/)

> This skill covers the `dioxus`, `dioxus-hooks`, `dioxus-signals`, `dioxus-stores`, `dioxus-router`, `dioxus-fullstack`, and `dioxus-document` crates.

## Standard Import

```rust
use dioxus::prelude::*;
```

## Quick Patterns

### Signal (reactive state)

```rust
let mut count = use_signal(|| 0);

// Read
count();              // clone value (callable syntax)
count.read();         // Ref<T> borrow
count.peek();         // read WITHOUT subscribing

// Write
count.set(5);         // replace
count += 1;           // arithmetic assignment
*count.write() = 10;  // mutable guard, triggers re-render on drop
```

`Signal<T>` is `Copy`. Reading subscribes to […]

## Standard Import

```rust
use leptos::prelude::*;
```

## Quick Patterns

### Signals (read-only + write-only pair)

```rust
let (count, set_count) = signal(0i32);       // ReadSignal + WriteSignal (both Copy)
set_count.set(5);
set_count.update(|n| *n += 1);
let val = count.get();                        // clone + subscribe
```

`ReadSignal<T>` is **read-only**. `WriteSignal<T>` is **write-only**. They are separate types.

For a combined read+write handle, use `RwSignal`:

```rust
let count = RwSignal::new(0i32);             // single handle, read + write
count.set(1); […]

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, […]

> AGENT

I found the likely Dioxus root cause: shell and close parts subscribe to `revision()` only, while selected/focus/message changes happen through other signals or machine messages. I’m adding focused regression tests that exercise rerendered props and shell-level attrs, then I’ll make the smallest reactivity fixes.

---
name: waiting-for-codex-review
description: Use immediately after pushing a PR to GitHub when Codex is configured to review the branch. Codex reviews asynchronously — it leaves a 👀 reaction on the PR while reviewing, drops the 👀 when the run finishes (either replacing it with 👍 if satisfied, or removing it and posting review threads if changes are needed). This skill defines the polling loop and the response workflow: wait for Codex's verdict, address any review threads it posts with the same rigor as `post-implementation-audit` (TDD + no coverage regression), commit, push, reply inline, resolve the thread, then keep waiting until 👍. Triggers on phrases like "wait for codex review", "what does codex say", "is codex done", "address the codex feedback", "check the PR reviews", or any post-push handoff where the user expects an automated reviewer's verdict. Invoke this skill even when the user does not explicitly name Codex — any GitHub PR where a 👀/👍 reaction signals an automated reviewer follows the same pattern.
---

  codex_eyes=$(echo "$reactions" | grep -E "codex.*:eyes$" || true)

When this script completes via Bash `run_in_background`, the single completion
notification fires. Recover the verdict with one `Read` on the task's output
file — the last line is `VERDICT=approval` or `VERDICT=needs_action threads=N`.
If the file's last line is something else (script crashed or hit the bash
timeout), apply the defensive re-check below.

### Defensive re-check: don't trust silence as "still reviewing"

Whether you use Bash `run_in_background` or `Monitor`, the delivery of
notifications back to the conversation is best-effort. If the runtime drops
the completion or change event, the loop sits waiting indefinitely for a
signal that already fired. The […]
